hook: Mud from Roman wells in Belgium yields ancient DNA that matches and extends excavated remains.
summary: DNA extracted from sediment in disused Roman wells at Harelbeke, Belgium, reproduced most crop and livestock signals known from excavation and added environmental species that older methods missed. It also placed a pig within the European mitochondrial lineage. This is one site, and counting taxa cannot show how much each food mattered.
title: Sedimentary ancient DNA expands bioarchaeological evidence and interpretation at Roman Harelbeke
